subject: Interop checklist & hyperscaler comparison — next steps
messages:
From: Diane Ho <diane.ho@bankcorp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment feasibility + hyperscaler comparison

Laura — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few asks before we schedule the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of BankCorp constraints:
- Must keep model inference within our VPC for any PII-sensitive workloads (regulatory).
- Control plane can be either customer-managed or a brokered model, but we need strong audit logs and KMS integration.
- Network must be restricted (no internet egress from the inference hosts).
- Air-gap for cert-scope: we may need an option to perform an offline install for an enclave subset (pilot).

Hyperscaler comparison questions (we asked legal/infra to list):
1) How does Redwood’s private deployment differ from running models on Hyperscaler A (managed endpoints + private networking) with respect to control plane traffic and telemetry?
2) Do you require long-lived outbound control-plane connections or do customers have an option for an agent/pull model?
3) If we need to fail over to hosted endpoints, what are the options for data residency and telemetry suppression?

Attachments: bankcorp-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 420KB) — high-level network posture.

Next steps we want from Redwood team: a concise checklist of tests you can run that map to our constraints (networking paths, control-plane flow, air-gap feasibility), an estimated timeline for each test, and a short comparison matrix vs Hyperscaler A/B/C for the control-plane model. Also please include any gating items that require infra changes on our side.

Thanks — Diane
Diane Ho
Principal Cloud Architect, BankCorp

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diane Ho <diane.ho@bankcorp.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility + hyperscaler comparison

Diane / Samir — thanks for the clear list, appreciated. Short response and a proposed plan below.

Quick answers up-front:
- Control plane traffic: Redwood Private supports both (1) a brokered control plane (managed by Redwood over an authenticated TLS tunnel) and (2) a customer-hosted control plane option where the control API sits inside the customer VPC and our agents connect via a customer-managed private path. We will call these "managed-controlplane" and "customer-controlplane" in the checklist.
- Outbound connections: we can support a pull/agent model (no long-lived unrestricted outbound tunnels) for the customer-controlplane option. Managed-controlplane uses a minimal outbound TLS connection for telemetry, but telemetry can be configured to mask payload identifiers.
- Failover: we can configure regional model fallbacks, but any fallback to hosted endpoints can be restricted to pseudonymous/aggregated telemetry only — and only with explicit account-level consent.

Proposed next steps (we’ll own delivery):
1) Internal scoping call (Redwood infra + R&D) — we will map the network flows in detail against your network diagram. (Target: 2026-10-03)
2) Build a short compatibility checklist that maps to your asks (control plane modes, KMS, audit logs, egress rules, air-gap install). Delivery: 2026-10-05 (ETA).
3) Run two lab tests: (A) agent-installed customer-controlplane behind strict egress rules; (B) offline installer for an enclosed pilot (air-gap). We’ll provide step-by-step runbooks. Proposed windows: 10/12 — 10/16.
4) Deliver comparison matrix vs Hyperscaler A/B (control-plane model, KMS support, audit granularity) by 10/05.

Can Karthik and Vivek weigh in on technical gating items below? I’ll consolidate final checklist and share a Drive link.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility + hyperscaler comparison

Laura — notes & quick tech plan. I’ll attach the compatibility CSV after this note.

Gating items we need from BankCorp (minimum):
- List of allowed outbound FQDNs/IPs from the inference hosts (if any). For agent pull model we need HTTPS egress to our artifact store or an internal mirror; for full air-gap we need a secure artifact bundle.
- KMS integration type: do you require HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM / on-prem HSM)? If on-prem HSM we’ll need the key exchange plan and service account details.
- Firewall/NAT behavior for long-lived connections (if you choose managed-controlplane).

Planned lab tests: 
A) Customer-controlplane (agent pull):
 - Deploy agent in a sandbox VPC with all egress blocked except to a single outgoing HTTPS proxy.
 - Validate model load, KV cache behavior, and token latency under constrained egress.
 - Outcome: pass/fail + instruction to reduce required egress to a minimal allowlist.

B) Air-gap/Offline install: 
 - Deliver signed artifact bundle (models + runtime) with a SHA256 manifest.
 - Validate local-only inference and KMS key signing for model loads (no outbound).
 - Outcome: feasibility + install runbook.

C) Control-plane telemetry audit: 
 - Exercise canaries with telemetry suppression flags and validate audit log completeness (request id, model id, timestamp) without payloads.

Marcus — can you confirm expected engineering effort for building the offline artifact bundle and ETA?

Attachment: controlplane-compat-matrix.csv (CSV, 18KB) — initial mapping vs Hyperscaler A/B/C for control-plane modes.

— Karthik
Staff PM, Infra Interop, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility + hyperscaler comparison

Adding ops/finops perspective — small notes for the customer and Diane: 
- Quantization/model variants: If BankCorp intends to use higher-throughput quantized variants we’ll surface per-token cost and latency differences in the checklist. Some quantized runtimes require different kernel support on the hardware side — we should flag this as an infra requirement.
- SLAs for offline pilot: an air-gap pilot will be run as an engineering engagement — we recommend a short committed window (2–3 weeks) and agree upfront on test criteria to avoid scope creep.
- Fall-back options: if we cannot complete an air-gap install in the pilot, we can propose an isolated managed-controlplane with telemetry suppression as a temporary step while we remediate.

Action: I’ll add a short cost/latency appendix to the checklist before we send to the customer.

— Vivek
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diane Ho <diane.ho@bankcorp.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Interop checklist & next steps (attached)

Diane / Samir — thanks again. Attached is the consolidated checklist and the initial compatibility matrix you requested. Highlights below and concrete next steps: 

High-level outcomes:
- Both control-plane modes supported: customer-controlplane (agent/pull) and managed-controlplane. We have explicit runbooks for both.
- Air-gap install is feasible as a pilot via an artifact bundle + SHA256 manifest; it requires an on-site installation step and HSM/KMS plan if you require on-prem keying.
- Minimal egress requirements for agent-pull: outbound HTTPS to a single allowlist entry or use of an internal artifact mirror.

Deliverables attached/links:
- redwood-private-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 55KB) — step-by-step tests, owner, estimated time.
- controlplane-compat-matrix.csv (CSV, 18KB) — comparison vs Hyperscaler A/B/C for control-plane models and telemetry.
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-bankcorp-checklist (contains runbooks and test templates).

Proposed schedule: 
- BankCorp network allowlist & KMS details due: 2026-10-08
- Lab test window (agent-pull + telemetry): 2026-10-12 – 2026-10-16
- Air-gap pilot planning call: 2026-10-13 (30m) — can you confirm availability?

Would you prefer a brief technical demo of the offline installer or to skip straight to the planning call?

Thanks — I’ll also open a HubSpot ticket for coordination and share the checklist there.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-private-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 55KB)
